1Outcome

Each participant requiring severe dysphagia management receives appropriate support that is relevant and proportionate to their individual needs and preferences.

2Quality indicators

(1)

Providers identify each participant requiring severe dysphagia management.

Our commitment: Policy C1, Policy C2.

(2)

With their consent, their individual severe dysphagia management needs are assessed by appropriately qualified health practitioners, including by practitioners conducting regular and timely reviews if needs change or difficulty is observed.

Our commitment: Policy C3, Policy C4. Proof: Form Q11, Form Q13, Form Q20, Form Q21, Form Q22.

(3)

Each participant requiring severe dysphagia management is involved in the assessment and development of their severe dysphagia management plan. The plan identifies:

  1. (a)their individual needs and preferences (such as for food, fluids, preparation techniques and feeding equipment); and
  2. (b)how risks, incidents and emergencies will be managed to ensure their wellbeing and safety, including by setting out any required actions and plans for escalation.

Our commitment: Policy C5, Policy C6, Policy C7. Proof: Form Q1, Form Q19, Form Q20.

(4)

Appropriate policies and procedures are in place in relation to the support provided to each participant requiring severe dysphagia management, including training plans for workers supporting them.

Our commitment: Policy C8, Policy C9, Policy C11, Policy C12. Proof: Form Q1, Form Q2, Form Q4, Form Q9, Form Q10, Form Q21.

(5)

Each worker responsible for providing severe dysphagia management to participants has received training, relating specifically to each participant’s needs, managing any severe dysphagia related incident and the high intensity support skills descriptor for severe dysphagia management, delivered by an appropriately qualified health practitioner with expertise in severe dysphagia management.

Our commitment: Policy C8. Proof: Form Q3, Form Q15, Form Q16.

docs.html:
1Purpose

This policy sets out what [Provider name] commits to. Its aim is that each participant who requires eats and drinks as safely, and as enjoyably, as their health allows. It is for participants, their families and advocates, our workers, and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Everyone who works for [Provider name]: employees, contractors, agency workers, volunteers and key personnel.
  • Every support where we prepare, serve or help with a participant's food or drink. This includes their home, a shared home, a day program, respite and the community.
  • Every participant whose swallowing difficulty is severe, or is suspected to be severe, until a says otherwise in writing.

Severe dysphagia management sits on top of mealtime management. POL-MTM-01 Mealtime Management Policy applies to the same participant. POL-HID-03 Enteral Feeding and Management Policy applies where the participant is also tube fed. POL-HID-01 High Intensity Daily Personal Activities Policy sets the commitments shared by every high intensity support.

3Commitments

C1

We will identify every participant who requires severe dysphagia management. We screen each participant for swallowing risk before their first meal with us. We screen again at every support review, and within 1 of any warning sign. A speech pathologist states in writing whether the participant requires it. We record the decision and keep one list of these participants.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 1.

C2

We will treat a participant as requiring severe dysphagia management from the moment we suspect it, until a speech pathologist says otherwise in writing. We get written from the participant's doctor or speech pathologist before the next meal. No worker or manager chooses a texture, a drink thickness or a food restriction.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 2.

C3

We will ask a speech pathologist with to assess swallowing, with the participant's consent. We also ask them to write or endorse the plan. We ask within 2 business days of consent, and on the same day when a sign is urgent. We ask other practitioners when the speech pathologist or the screen advises.

Answers: Legislation (2). How we do it: Procedure step 3, Procedure step 4.

C4

We will ask the speech pathologist to review the assessment and the plan at least every 12 months, or by the earlier date they set. We also ask for a review within 1 business day of any change or difficulty a worker sees. Examples are choking, coughing that stops a meal, a chest infection, a hospital stay, an unplanned weight change, a new medicine that the pharmacist or prescriber says may affect swallowing or alertness, and a change in alertness. Other medicine changes go to the pharmacist first.

Answers: Legislation (2). How we do it: Procedure step 29.

C5

We will involve each participant in their assessment and their plan, in their usual way of communicating, and record their consent. We respect and record an to eat or drink differently from the plan. We never withdraw support because of that choice.

Answers: Legislation (3), Legislation (3)(a). How we do it: Procedure step 3, Procedure step 5, Procedure step 7, Procedure step 8, Procedure step 14.

C6

We will support each participant under one written plan that a speech pathologist wrote or endorsed. It states their needs and preferences: food and drink levels, preparation and testing, equipment, position, pace, supervision, mouth care, medicines, and what they like. We do not use a plan until a practitioner has answered each of those points.

Answers: Legislation (3), Legislation (3)(a). How we do it: Procedure step 6.

C7

We will make sure each plan sets out how risks, incidents and emergencies are managed for that participant. It names the signs to watch for and what the worker does for each. It says when to call 000, who to phone and how fast. It also says what happens before the next meal after an event.

Answers: Legislation (3), Legislation (3)(b). How we do it: Procedure step 6, Procedure step 19.

C8

We will train each worker for each participant before they support a meal. A speech pathologist with expertise in severe dysphagia management gives the training and signs the worker off. Where the speech pathologist nominates them, another appropriately qualified health practitioner with documented expertise in severe dysphagia management may train and sign off instead. The training covers the participant's needs, how to manage a incident, and the NDIS Commission's skills descriptor. A sign-off lapses after 3 months without supporting the participant, and when the clinical content of the plan changes (a new review date or phone number does not lapse it). We train and sign off again when it lapses, and every 12 months. We roster only signed-off workers to a meal.

Answers: Legislation (4), Legislation (5). How we do it: Procedure step 10, Procedure step 11, Procedure step 12.

C9

We will support every meal, snack and the same way. The worker reads the plan and prepares to the stated levels. They test, position the participant, help at the set pace and watch for signs. They keep the participant upright afterwards and record the meal on the same day.

Answers: Legislation (3)(a), Legislation (4). How we do it: Procedure step 13, Procedure step 14, Procedure step 15, Procedure step 16, Procedure step 17, Procedure step 18, Procedure step 19, Procedure step 20, Procedure step 21, Procedure step 22.

C10

We will respond to every choking event, and every sign that food or drink went into the lungs. The response is first aid, a 000 call where needed, an incident report, and a medical review the same day after choking that needed first aid and after any sign that food or drink went into the lungs: a wet or gurgly voice, a change of colour, shortness of breath, or chest signs in the hours or days after a meal. We tell the speech pathologist the same day. We give nothing more by mouth except as the participant's plan allows while advice is sought. We follow our incident procedures. We notify the NDIS Commission within 24 hours of becoming aware where the incident involves the death, serious injury, abuse or neglect, unlawful sexual or physical contact or sexual misconduct of a participant, or an unauthorised restrictive practice that resulted in harm; otherwise within 5 business days.

Answers: Legislation (3)(b). How we do it: Procedure step 23, Procedure step 24, Procedure step 25, Procedure step 26, Procedure step 27.

C11

We will keep the current plan at every place the participant eats or drinks, where a worker can find it in under a minute. We remove older versions the same day. With consent, we send the plan with the participant to hospital and to other services. We treat discharge instructions as interim precautions.

Answers: Legislation (4). How we do it: Procedure step 9, Procedure step 30.

C12

We will check each participant's meal records every week for completeness, and the will read a sample of each participant's records every month, and every record after an incident or a plan change, and act on what they show. We report trends in choking and swallowing incidents to the governing body every 3 months.

Answers: Legislation (4). How we do it: Procedure step 28.

4Ground rules

G1

The participant decides what they eat and drink. We give information, the speech pathologist's advice and safe support. We never force, trick or hold a person to make them eat. Food and drink are never a reward or a punishment.

G2

Only health practitioners assess a participant, set the levels, and write or change the plan. Decision table 4 in PRO-HID-03 Severe Dysphagia Management Procedure sets who may do each task. A worker or a manager never fills a gap in a plan.

G3

One plan governs at the table: the participant's Mealtime Management Plan (FRM-MTM-01), written or endorsed by a speech pathologist. This policy and PRO-HID-03 add what that plan must hold for severe dysphagia. There is no second plan.

G4

Any amount, level, time or rate comes from the practitioner and sits in the participant's own plan. Thickener, mouthful size, time upright and fluid targets are examples. Our documents never print one as a general rule.

G5

We do not crush, split, open or mix a medicine for a participant with swallowing difficulty. The exception is written advice from the prescriber or a pharmacist, kept in the plan.

G6

A speech pathologist trains each worker and signs them off. Where the speech pathologist nominates them, another appropriately qualified health practitioner with documented expertise in severe dysphagia management may do so. A manager cannot sign off a worker. A sole trader cannot sign off themselves.

G7

We take on a participant who requires severe dysphagia management only while our certificate of registration lists it (Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 2, clause 4A(1)). We must also keep two signed-off people for them, so that one absence leaves no gap. A sole trader meets this only where a named second person, another provider's worker or a supporter the plan names, has been trained and by the speech pathologist and is on the sign-off list before we take on the participant. If we cannot, we say so at once, help the participant find a provider who can, and keep to the interim precautions until they have.

G8

Every choking event, near choking event or sign that food or drink went into the lungs is an incident under POL-INC-01 Incident Management Policy.

G9

Limiting a participant's access to food or drink to manage their behaviour can be a regulated restrictive practice. We use it only as PRO-BSP-02 Regulated Restrictive Practices Procedure allows. A speech pathologist's advice about safe textures is clinical advice, not a restrictive practice.

G10

In a small provider one person may hold several roles. The Clinical Lead is a registered nurse, or another health practitioner whose scope covers the support, whom we engage to oversee high intensity supports. A sole trader cannot be their own Clinical Lead and engages one. The Service Manager holds the administrative tasks only. Every clinical decision still comes from the speech pathologist, the participant's doctor or the Clinical Lead. A concern about a sole trader goes to the independent contact for concerns named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register.

377 words
severe dysphagia
difficulty swallowing, chewing or biting that a speech pathologist or doctor says puts the participant at serious risk. The risks are choking, food or drink going into the lungs, poor nutrition and dehydration.
severe dysphagia management
the support a participant with severe dysphagia needs to eat and drink safely. It includes the plan, trained workers, support at every meal and the response to choking.
plan
the participant's Mealtime Management Plan (FRM-MTM-01), written or endorsed by a speech pathologist, with the extra points PRO-HID-03 requires for severe dysphagia.
speech pathologist
a health practitioner who assesses swallowing and holds the credential of their professional body. Where this policy says a speech pathologist trains or signs off a worker, it also means another appropriately qualified health practitioner with documented expertise in severe dysphagia management whom the speech pathologist nominates.
expertise in severe dysphagia management
regular clinical work with people who have severe dysphagia. The practitioner shows it in a written statement of how long, where and with whom, kept in REG-HID-02.
signed off
a speech pathologist has watched the worker carry out this participant's plan correctly, and the worker has signed that they can follow it. A sign-off covers one participant. It lapses after 3 months without supporting the participant, and when the clinical content of the plan changes; a new review date or phone number does not lapse it.
interim precautions
written advice from the participant's doctor or speech pathologist about meals until the plan is in place.
drink round
any drink offered between meals. Every drink round is supported and recorded the same way as a meal.
aspiration
food, drink or saliva going into the lungs. It can happen without a cough.
IDDSI
the International Dysphagia Diet Standardisation Initiative framework. It names food textures and drink thicknesses by number.
informed choice
a decision the participant makes after the risks and options are explained in a way they understand.
Clinical Lead
a registered nurse, or another health practitioner whose scope covers the support, whom [Provider name] engages to oversee high intensity supports. A sole trader cannot be their own Clinical Lead and engages one.
business day
a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

1Purpose

The result: every participant who requires is found and assessed by a . Trained workers support them at every meal, under one written made with them. Choking, and food or drink going into the lungs, get the right response straight away.

This procedure gives effect to POL-HID-04 Severe Dysphagia Management Policy, C1 to C12.

It sits on top of PRO-MTM-01 Mealtime Management Procedure. Both apply to this participant. There is one plan at the table: FRM-MTM-01 Mealtime Management Plan, with the extra points in Decision table 2.

Where a Record line names a form or register that is not yet a Rise template, record the same facts in the participant's file under the same heading until it is.

2When and who

Start this procedure:

  • when the mealtime screen (FRM-MTM-02 Nutrition and Swallowing Risk Screen) or a practitioner's report shows that is known or suspected, from step 1
  • at every support plan review and after any warning sign, from step 1
  • at every meal, snack and for a participant who requires severe dysphagia management, from step 13.

Severe dysphagia is difficulty swallowing, chewing or biting that a speech pathologist or doctor says puts the participant at serious risk. The risks are choking, food or drink going into the lungs, poor nutrition and dehydration. We never decide how severe it is ourselves.

Who acts:

  • The decides and records who requires severe dysphagia management. They arrange assessment, the plan check, training and reviews. They read a sample of each participant's meal records every month, and every record after an incident or a plan change. The Clinical Lead is a registered nurse, or another health practitioner whose scope covers the support, whom [Provider name] engages to oversee high intensity supports.
  • The speech pathologist assesses swallowing and writes or endorses the plan. They train workers and sign them off, or nominate another appropriately qualified health practitioner with documented to do so. They must have expertise in severe dysphagia management.
  • Other practitioners add to the plan: a dietitian, an occupational therapist, a physiotherapist, the participant's doctor, a pharmacist and a dentist.
  • The Service Manager takes the participant's consent, rosters signed-off workers, keeps REG-HID-01 and REG-HID-02, checks every shift's meal records for completeness each week, puts the plan in place and sends it with the participant.
  • The worker at the meal prepares, tests, helps, watches and records.
  • The on-call manager takes calls at any meal. In office hours this is the Service Manager. After hours it is the rostered manager.
  • The Quality Manager, as the authorised notifier, decides whether an event is a reportable incident and notifies the NDIS Commission.

In a small provider one person may hold several of these roles. A sole trader is the Service Manager and the worker at the meal. A sole trader cannot be their own Clinical Lead and engages one. A sole trader cannot sign off their own competency; the speech pathologist does that. Before you take on the participant, a named second person, another provider's worker or a supporter the plan names, must be trained and by the speech pathologist and on the sign-off list, so that a sole trader who is ill leaves a signed-off person to cover the meal. Where a step says to phone a manager, a sole trader writes down the time and phones the Clinical Lead, the speech pathologist or the participant's doctor directly. A concern about a sole trader goes to the independent contact for concerns named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register.

3Before you start

Workers at a meal:

  • You are on the sign-off list kept with the plan.
  • Your first aid and CPR training is current: CPR within the last 12 months and first aid within the last 3 years.
  • You know where the participant's plan is kept.
  • You know the on-call number: [on-call number].
  • You have the thickener, the equipment and the test tools the plan names.

Clinical Lead:

  • You can open REG-HID-02 High Intensity Supports Register and REG-HID-01 High Intensity Training and Competency Register.
  • You know how to reach the participant's speech pathologist, doctor, dietitian and pharmacist.

Service Manager:

  • You can open the roster and the sign-off list for each participant.
  • You hold the participant's consent record (FRM-INF-01) and their communication preferences (FRM-RGT-01).

4Watch out

  • Choking can kill within minutes. If the participant cannot cough, speak or breathe, call 000 before you call a manager.
  • No cough does not mean safe. Food and drink can go into the lungs without a cough. The harm shows hours or days later as a chest infection. Follow the plan even when the participant seems fine.
  • Never choose or change a texture, a thickness, a position or the plan. Only the speech pathologist does. The wrong level can block the airway or put food or drink into the lungs.
  • A drowsy participant cannot protect their airway. Food, drink or a medicine given by mouth to a drowsy person can go into the lungs.
  • Texture changes as food cools, stands or is reheated. A meal that passed the test an hour ago can fail now.
  • Some foods hide thin liquid. Ice cream, jelly, juicy fruit and soup with pieces turn to thin liquid in the mouth. The plan lists what to avoid.
  • A crushed or mixed medicine can harm. Only the prescriber or a pharmacist can say a medicine may be altered, in writing.
  • Dry thickener powder is a choking hazard. Store it where the plan says.
  • A worker who is not signed off must not help at a meal. They do not know this participant's needs or the choking response.
  • Force is never used. Forcing food, or holding a person to feed them, is abuse.

5Steps

Find who requires severe dysphagia management

Step 1

The Clinical Lead

Decide whether the participant requires severe dysphagia management.

Use Decision table 1. Start with the screen result, any practitioner's report, hospital papers and what workers have seen at meals. If the participant agrees, ask their speech pathologist to state in writing whether they require severe dysphagia management. Write the decision, the date, the name and profession of the person who made it, and the report it rests on. Add the participant to the list of participants who require it, and to their risk assessment (FRM-SUP-06 Participant Risk Assessment and Management Plan). Screen again at every support plan review.

Result
We know who requires severe dysphagia management, who said so and when.
Record
REG-HID-02. FRM-SUP-06
Time limit
Within 1 of a screen result, a report or a warning sign (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C1.

Step 2

Warning. A texture or thickness chosen by a worker or a manager can cause choking, or put food or drink into the lungs.

The Clinical Lead

If severe dysphagia is required or suspected, and no plan is in place:

Get written from the participant's doctor or speech pathologist.

Phone the practitioner, with the participant if they agree. Write their name, profession, the date and time, and their advice. Read each food and drink level back to them by its number and name, and each other precaution in full, and wait for them to confirm. Ask them to send written confirmation (a secure message or email from the practice counts as written) before the next business day; until it arrives, workers follow the advice as read back. If the advice is "no change", write that. If advice is already on the participant's file, check it is current. Until you have advice, the participant keeps the food and drink they have now. Give nothing by mouth, and get health advice the same day, in three cases. One: the participant choked and has not been checked. Two: they cannot stay awake. Three: they cannot swallow their saliva or medicines. Call 000 if they are unwell now. Brief each worker before their next meal with the participant, and record the briefing: the worker, the date, who briefed them and the advice they read. Only briefed workers support meals until the plan takes effect.

Result
Every worker has written clinical advice for every meal until the plan is in place.

REG-HID-02. A dated interim precautions sheet, filed with the plan and not written into it

Before the next meal we support. The same day when the participant choked, cannot stay awake or cannot swallow saliva or medicines. Written confirmation from the practitioner before the next business day (our standard)

At every meal

The worker at the meal

Read the participant's current plan and the handover.

You know what this participant needs at this meal.

FRM-HID-07 Q1, Q2 and Q3

Before you prepare anything (our standard)

The worker at the meal

Ask the participant how they are and what they want from the meal.

Use their usual way of communicating. Ask where they want to eat, who with and what they want from the menu. The participant has a say in their meal, and you know of any change before you start.

Test the food and the drink the way the plan says.

The plan names each test and what a pass looks like. Test at serving temperature. Test again after reheating or standing. Test bought and delivered meals as well. If the food or drink fails, or you are unsure, do not serve it. Make it again, or phone the on-call manager.

Only food and drink at the right level reach the participant.

FRM-HID-07 Q5 and Q6

The worker at the meal

Check that the participant is alert and positioned as the plan says.

The plan describes what alert looks like. If the participant is drowsy, give nothing by mouth. Wait as the plan says, then check again. The participant is ready to eat and drink safely.

FRM-HID-07 Q7 and Q8

Before the first mouthful (our standard)

The worker at the meal

Help the participant eat and drink the way the plan says.

Sit at eye level and give the meal your full attention. Put your phone away. Say what each food is. Keep the pace, the mouthful size and the prompts the plan sets. Check the mouth is empty before the next mouthful. Give a drink to wash food down only if the plan says so. Use a straw only if the plan allows it. Do not tip the head back to give food or drink unless the plan says so. Stay with the participant for the whole meal, as close as the plan sets. Never rush, force or hold. The participant eats and drinks safely at their own pace, with dignity.
Record
FRM-HID-07 Q9, Q10 and Q11
Time limit
At each meal (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C9. Written on: Form Q9, Form Q10, Form Q11.

The worker at the meal

If you see any sign in Decision table 3:

The participant gets no more food or drink while at risk, and a manager knows.

FRM-HID-07 Q13 and Q14

Straight away. Phone the on-call manager as soon as the participant is safe (our standard)

The medicine is taken in the form the pharmacist or prescriber confirmed, or it is not given and someone is told.

FRM-HID-07 Q12. FRM-MED-01

With the meal, as the medication chart sets (our standard)

The participant finishes the meal clean, comfortable and safe.

FRM-HID-07 Q17, Q18 and Q19

Straight after the meal, for as long as the plan sets (our standard)

The Clinical Lead and the speech pathologist can see how each meal went.

FRM-HID-07 Q20

Before your shift ends (our standard)

Choking, and food or drink going into the lungs

Step 23

Warning. A person who cannot cough, speak or breathe can die within minutes.

The worker at the meal

If the participant cannot cough, speak or breathe, is clutching their throat, or is turning blue or grey:

Call 000.

Put the phone on speaker. Say "choking" and give the address. Stay on the line and follow the operator. If another person is there, they phone while you give first aid. Do not wait for a manager.

Result
An ambulance is coming.
Record
FRM-HID-07 Q15
Time limit
Straight away (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C10. Written on: Form Q15.

Step 24

The worker at the meal

If the participant cannot cough, speak or breathe:

Give choking first aid the way you were trained.

Use the technique you were trained in for the participant's age and size. The plan names any change for this participant, such as for a wheelchair or a body shape. Otherwise give up to 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades, and check after each one. If the airway is still blocked, give up to 5 chest thrusts, and check after each one. Keep going until the airway clears or help arrives. If the participant stops responding and is not breathing normally, start CPR. Use a defibrillator if there is one. Do not sweep the mouth unless you can see the food. Use equipment such as oral suction only if you are signed off for it for this participant.

Result
The airway is cleared, or first aid continues until paramedics take over.
Record
FRM-HID-07 Q15
Time limit
Straight away (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C10. Written on: Form Q15.

Step 25

The worker at the meal

If the participant choked, had a coughing fit that stopped the meal, or may have breathed in food or drink:

Give nothing more by mouth until you have health advice, except what the plan allows while advice is sought.

Keep the participant upright and stay with them. Watch for the signs in Decision table 3 for the rest of your shift. Phone the on-call manager. They tell the speech pathologist the same day, and get advice from them or from the participant's doctor. Where the plan does not say, give nothing more by mouth and tell the on-call manager about any drink or medicine that is due; they get advice before it is due. Result
The participant is not put at risk again before a health professional has checked.
Record
FRM-HID-07 Q14. FRM-SUP-08. REG-HID-02

Until that advice is given, and before the participant next eats or drinks (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C10. Written on: Form Q14.

Step 26

The worker at the meal

If the participant choked, nearly choked or may have breathed in food or drink:

A manager knows, and the event is in the incident system.

FRM-INC-01. FRM-HID-07 Q16

The on-call manager

The participant has been checked, and any harm is treated early.

FRM-INC-01. REG-HID-02

The same day, before the participant next eats or drinks (our standard)

How the participant is seated or positioned to eat and drink, the cups, cutlery and plates, and how long they stay upright afterwardsThe speech pathologist. An occupational therapist or physiotherapist for seating
The level of help and supervision, how close the worker stays, the pace, the mouthful size, how to check the mouth is empty and when the meal stopsThe speech pathologist
How alert the participant must be before a meal starts, and what the worker does if they are notThe speech pathologist
The mouth care before and after meals, and how dentures are cleaned and storedThe speech pathologist. A dentist if teeth or dentures are the concern
How each medicine is taken: its form, the fluid it is taken with and that fluid's thickness, confirmed in writingThe prescriber or a pharmacist
What the participant likes and dislikes, their culture and beliefs about food, where, when and with whom they eat, and how they show hunger, thirst, enjoyment, refusal and distressThe participant, with the Clinical Lead. The speech pathologist then checks what is safe
The signs that food or drink has gone into the lungs, and the signs of decline such as weight loss, dehydration and repeated chest infections, each with what the worker does, who is phoned and how fastThe speech pathologist and the participant's doctor
The emergency steps for this participant: any change to choking first aid, when to call 000, who to phone in what order, and the information that goes with the participant to hospitalThe speech pathologist and the participant's doctor
What happens after a choking or coughing event before the next meal or drink: who must be asked, which fluids may be given while waiting, and how a medicine that falls due is handledThe speech pathologist
Any equipment that only a signed-off worker may use, such as oral suction, who trains and signs off workers in it, and what a worker who is not signed off does insteadThe speech pathologist
The linked health risks and the practitioner's instruction for each: allergy and anaphylaxis, diabetes, reflux, weight loss or gain, dehydration, and mouth or dental problemsThe speech pathologist, the dietitian or the participant's doctor
What workers record and report: the triggers for low food, low fluids and weight change, and how often the participant is weighed and by whomThe speech pathologist and the dietitian
Who else is in the participant's health team, with contact details: the doctor, the dietitian, a nurse, a pharmacist and any other practitionerThe Clinical Lead, from the participant
How the participant took part, who consented and any with its safeguardsThe Service Manager and the Clinical Lead, from steps 5, 7 and 8
The review due date, no later than 12 months after the assessment, the reasons for an earlier review, and the practitioner's contact detailsThe speech pathologist

Decision table 3: Signs at and after a meal

If you seeThen
Coughing, and the participant can still cough, speak or breatheStop the meal and take the food and drink away. Encourage them to keep coughing. Stay with them. Give no back blows and no drink. If the cough turns weak or silent, go to step 23. Then follow step 25 and step 26
The participant cannot cough, speak or breathe, clutches their throat or turns blue or greyGo to step 23 now
A wet or gurgly voice, watery eyes, noisy breathing, shortness of breath or a change of colourStop the meal. Keep the participant upright. Give nothing more. Call 000 if breathing is hard or does not settle. Phone the on-call manager, who arranges a medical review the same day (step 27). Then follow step 25 and step 26
Food left in the mouthStop offering more. Use the prompts the plan sets. Give a drink only if the plan says so. Check the mouth is clear before you leave
The participant becomes drowsy or falls asleepStop the meal. Check the mouth is empty. Give nothing by mouth. Try again when they are alert, as the plan says. Phone the on-call manager if a meal or a medicine will be missed
The participant refuses the meal, or part of itRespect the refusal. Do not press or coax. Offer another choice at the same level, and offer again later. Record it. If meals keep being refused, phone the on-call manager in the same shift
The participant asks for food or drink the plan says to avoidExplain the risk in their usual way of communicating. Offer the nearest safe choice. Do not take food by force or hold them back. Unless step 8 has recorded the choice, do not prepare or hand it over. Stay close and be ready to give first aid. Tell the Clinical Lead in the same shift
More drooling than usual, or the participant cannot swallow their salivaGive nothing by mouth. Keep the participant upright. Phone the on-call manager, who gets advice the same day. Call 000 if breathing is hard
Repeated throat clearing, pain when swallowing, or food or drink coming from the noseStop the meal. Give nothing more. Phone the on-call manager in the same shift. The Clinical Lead asks for a plan review (step 29)
Vomiting, or food coming back upStop the meal. Keep the participant upright, or on their side if they are lying down. Give nothing more. Phone the on-call manager. Call 000 if breathing is affected
Fever, a wet or rattly chest, a new cough, fast breathing or more tiredness than usual in the hours or days after a mealPhone the on-call manager straight away. Call 000 if breathing is hard. Otherwise a doctor sees the participant the same day (step 27). The Clinical Lead asks for a plan review (step 29)
Hives, swelling of the lips, face or tongue, wheezing or collapse after eatingFollow the participant's allergy action plan. Call 000
The participant eats or drinks much less over several meals, or a trigger in the plan for food, fluids or weight is metPhone the on-call manager in the same shift. The Clinical Lead asks the dietitian or the speech pathologist for advice the same day
Anything else that worries youStop the meal and stay with the participant. Phone the on-call manager. If you are not sure it is safe, call 000

Decision table 4: Who may do what

If the task isThen it is done by
Noticing and reporting a signEvery worker
Choking first aidAny worker with current first aid and CPR training (CPR within 12 months, first aid within 3 years)
Preparing food and drink to a level, testing, positioning, helping at the meal and mouth care, as the plan setsA worker signed off for this participant
Giving a medicine in the form the plan statesA worker signed off for this participant and for medicines under PRO-MED-01 Management of Medication Procedure
Using equipment the plan names, such as oral suctionOnly a worker whom the plan's practitioner has named, trained and signed off for that equipment for this participant. Any other worker calls 000 instead
Tube feedingA worker trained and signed off under PRO-HID-02 Enteral Feeding and Management Procedure
Deciding that a participant requires severe dysphagia managementA speech pathologist says so in writing. The Clinical Lead records it
Assessing swallowing. Setting the food and drink levels, the thickener, the tests, the position, the supervision and what to do for each signA speech pathologist only
Training workers and signing them offA speech pathologist with expertise in severe dysphagia management, or another appropriately qualified health practitioner with documented expertise whom the speech pathologist nominates
Assessing nutrition. Setting a diet, a target or a supplementA dietitian, or the participant's doctor
Assessing seating. Prescribing mealtime equipmentAn occupational therapist or a physiotherapist
Changing how a medicine is takenThe prescriber or a pharmacist, in writing
Finding the cause of a chest sign and treating itA doctor or paramedics
Changing anything in the planThe speech pathologist who wrote it. Never a worker or a manager

7If it goes wrong

IfThen
You cannot find the plan at the place of the mealDo not guess. Phone the on-call manager before you prepare anything. They read the plan to you from the participant's file and send a copy. The Service Manager replaces the copy that day
The review date on the plan has passedFollow the plan. Tell the Clinical Lead in the same shift. The Clinical Lead asks the speech pathologist within 1 business day whether the plan stands until the review
You are not signed off, or the signed-off worker is absentDo not start the meal on your own judgement. Phone the on-call manager. They send a signed-off worker and tell the participant about the delay. If none can arrive within 1 hour of the mealtime, or a medicine depends on the meal, the on-call manager gets advice from the speech pathologist or the participant's doctor on what is safe. Report it as a missed or failed support under PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure
The food or drink fails the test, or you are unsureDo not serve it. Make it again. If it still fails, phone the on-call manager and offer an item the menu shows at the right level
The thickener or a piece of equipment has run out or is missingDo not swap in another product or guess an amount. Phone the on-call manager, who arranges supply that day. If the participant cannot have a safe drink before the next drink the plan schedules, the on-call manager gets health advice
The participant refuses the assessment, the review or the planRespect the decision. Explain the risk and offer an advocate. Record it on the consent record and complete FRM-RSK-01 Risk Assessment Form. Keep supporting them under the interim precautions. Ask again at the next support plan review, or sooner if signs get worse. An urgent sign still needs same day health advice
There is no appointment date after 10 business days, or the wait is longer than 4 weeksThe Clinical Lead asks the participant's doctor and support coordinator for another route, including a hospital or community dysphagia service. The interim precautions are checked with the doctor every 4 weeks. The Clinical Lead tells the Quality Manager, who adds the risk to REG-RSK-01 Risk Register
The speech pathologist cannot show expertise in severe dysphagia managementDo not use them to train workers or sign off. Ask for a referral to a speech pathologist who does. Keep the interim precautions. Record what you asked for and the answer
The trainer is not available when a worker is neededThe worker does not support meals. Keep other signed-off workers on the roster. Ask the speech pathologist to nominate another appropriately qualified health practitioner with documented expertise, or for a live video session where a reassessment is due. If no signed-off worker can cover a meal, follow the row for an absent worker
Our certificate of registration does not list severe dysphagia management, or we cannot keep two signed-off people for the participantTell the participant and the people they choose the same day, in their usual way of communicating. Help them find a provider who can, with their support coordinator. Keep to the interim precautions and use only briefed workers until the handover. Do not leave the participant without a safe meal. Tell the Chief Executive
The 12 month review will be lateKeep following the plan. Ask the speech pathologist in writing whether it stands until the review. Record the answer in REG-HID-02. Tell the Quality Manager
The participant comes home from hospital with new instructionsTreat the discharge instructions as interim precautions (step 2). Brief each worker before their next meal with the participant. Ask for a plan review within 1 business day (step 29)
Family or another supporter gives food the plan says to avoidDo not argue at the table. Stay close and be ready to give first aid. Tell the Clinical Lead in the same shift. With the participant's consent, the Clinical Lead offers that person the speech pathologist's training
You are out with the participant, and the venue cannot serve the right levelDo not serve it and do not improvise. Offer what you brought, or phone the on-call manager. Never serve a food or a drink you cannot test
The participant's goals change to comfort, for example at the end of lifeDo not change anything yourself. The Clinical Lead asks the speech pathologist and the participant's doctor to review the plan with the participant and their decision maker. PRO-RGT-05 Advance Care Planning Procedure applies; it is not yet written, so until it is the Clinical Lead records the request and the practitioners' advice in the participant's file
A colleague rushes, forces, withholds food, serves the wrong level or is not signed offReport it to the Clinical Lead in the same shift. It is an incident, and it may be abuse or neglect. PRO-SGD-01 Violence, Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation and Discrimination Procedure applies. Nobody may punish you for reporting
The concern is about the Clinical Lead or the Service ManagerPhone the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive or a sole trader, phone the independent contact for concerns in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. You can always phone the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544
You do not feel safe to start a mealSay so to the on-call manager at once. Nobody is punished for it. They send a signed-off worker or get health advice
The system is downUse the paper copy of FRM-HID-07 and the printed plan. Enter the record when the system is back

8Done means

  • The participant is on the list of participants who require severe dysphagia management, with the decision, the date and who made it, in REG-HID-02.
  • Written interim precautions were in place from the day we suspected severe dysphagia until the plan took effect.
  • The participant's consent, and any informed choice, are on their file.
  • A speech pathologist with expertise in severe dysphagia management wrote or endorsed the plan, and the plan answers every point in Decision table 2.
  • The current plan is at every place the participant eats or drinks, and no older version is in use.
  • Every worker who supports their meals is signed off and listed in REG-HID-01.
  • Every meal has a record in FRM-HID-07. The Service Manager has checked each week's records for completeness, and the Clinical Lead has read the monthly sample and every record after an incident or a plan change.
  • Every choking event, or sign of food or drink in the lungs, has an incident report and a medical review. It also has a request for a plan review.
  • The speech pathologist has reviewed the assessment and the plan within 12 months.

9Quick card

145 words
  • If the participant cannot cough, speak or breathe, call 000. (step 23)
  • Give choking first aid the way you were trained: back blows, then chest thrusts. (step 24)
  • Stop the meal at any sign. Stay with the participant. (step 19)
  • After choking or a coughing fit that stops a meal, give nothing more by mouth, except what the plan allows, until you have advice. (step 25)
  • Start only if you are signed off for this participant. Read the current plan first. (step 13)
  • Prepare to the plan's levels. Never change a texture or a thickness yourself. (step 15)
  • Test the food and the drink before every serve. If unsure, do not serve. (step 16)
  • Check the participant is awake and positioned as the plan says. (step 17)
  • Stay with them, keep them upright after the meal, and record it before your shift ends. (step 22)

form.intro:
This record shows how each meal went for one participant who requires . The worker at the meal completes it at every meal, snack and , answering only the questions the list below sets for that use. The Service Manager checks it every week for completeness. The Clinical Lead reads a sample every month, and every record after an incident or a plan change.

For this participant, this record takes the place of the mealtime record in the Mealtime Management Plan (FRM-MTM-01). Do not complete both. FRM-MTM-01 is not yet a Rise template; until it is, this record is the participant's only meal record.

Complete one entry for each use. Question 1 is completed once per page, and question 3 once per page for each worker who writes on it. Also complete an entry when you see a sign between meals, such as a fever or a wet cough after an earlier meal. When, and which questions to complete:

  • A meal (breakfast, lunch, dinner or supper): questions 2, 4 to 13, then 14 to 16 when a sign other than "none" is ticked, then 17 to 20.
  • A snack: questions 2, 4, 5 or 6 as served, 9, 13, then 14 to 16 when a sign is ticked, then 18.
  • A drink round: questions 2, 4, 6, 9, 13, then 14 to 16 when a sign is ticked, then 18.
  • A sign seen between meals: questions 2 and 13 to 16.
  • The first meal of each day: also the weight at question 1 where the plan asks for it. The last entry of the day: also the day's drink total at question 9 where the plan sets a fluid target.
  • Sections A to E: the worker at the meal completes these, while they work and before their shift ends.
  • Section F: the Service Manager completes question 21 every week. The Clinical Lead completes questions 21 and 22 every month, and after every incident or plan change.

Have ready: the participant's current plan, the handover, and the list of workers for this participant. The list is kept with the plan.

Do not change the plan and do not guess an answer the plan should give. If the plan does not say, write "not in the plan". Phone the on-call manager before you serve.

What happens next: PRO-HID-03 Severe Dysphagia Management Procedure sets every step. A sign at a meal goes to the on-call manager in the same shift. The Clinical Lead asks the for a review when the records show a problem. Where this record names a form or register that is not yet a Rise template, the same facts are recorded in the participant's file under the same heading until it is.

When systems are down, use the paper copy. Paper copies are kept at [location at each site].
form.privacy:
We collect this information to help you eat and drink safely and enjoy your meals. It includes health information about you.

The workers who support your meals read it. So do the Clinical Lead, your speech pathologist and your doctor. With your consent, we give a copy to other people who support your meals, such as a day program or your family.

You can ask to see what we hold about you and ask us to correct it. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect this record.
form.after:
• Worker: complete Sections A to E before your shift ends (our standard). Phone the on-call manager, or the Clinical Lead in office hours, in the same shift about any sign at question 13 (our standard).
  • On-call manager: get advice from the speech pathologist or the participant's doctor the same day when question 13 shows a sign (our standard). Get it before the participant next eats or drinks if they choked (our standard).
  • Service Manager: check each participant's records every week for completeness and complete question 21 (our standard). Clinical Lead: read a sample of each participant's records every month, and every record after an incident or a plan change, and complete questions 21 and 22 (our standard). Copy any entry named in the question protocol to REG-HID-02 High Intensity Supports Register.
  • Clinical Lead: send the records to the speech pathologist at each review, with the participant's consent (our standard). Send them at any other time a trigger in the plan is met.
  • Quality Manager: sample 10 meal records for each participant at each internal audit under PRO-QMS-03 Internal Audit and Self-Assessment Procedure (our standard).
  • The records stay on the participant's file. They are kept for 7 years (NDIS Act 2013, section 45B, from 27 August 2026: records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years). The health records law of [state or territory] can require longer, and so can a record about a child. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how they are stored and protected.
